author: Forbes
description:
It took North Korean hackers months to penetrate Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, and about 20 minutes to steal more than $6.3 billion. The operation began well before the October 29 heist, with attackers using compromised software and a fake job interview to gain access to employees’ computers. From there, they worked their way through internal systems until they could authorize transactions from the exchange’s digital wallets.

The largest theft in crypto history underscored a troubling reality for an industry that has spent years defending against cybercriminals. Hackers are increasingly finding ways around the code that protects digital assets by targeting the people and infrastructure that control them, and AI is making such attacks cheaper and easier to execute, allowing criminals to mount sophisticated exploits that once required considerable time and exceptional technical skill.

Hackers have stolen a record $8.7 billion in cryptocurrency via 325 incidents
title: After Binance’s $6 Billion Burglary, AI-Fueled Hacks Are Now Crypto’s Biggest Threat
